scope: Read-only follow-up; no compilation, source edits, dependency updates, push, PR, or external messages performed for this investigation.

conclusion.status: Unresolved compiler/source interaction; diagnostic origin and likely mechanism identified, not certified harmless
conclusion.packaging_independence: The same ten diagnostics occur when the unchanged pinned OpenCC source is built directly by the official host-tools1 configuration, before the Gradle wrapper task. They are independent of the missing regional-dictionary packaging defect. This PR exposes that host compilation path and must disclose the warnings; it does not fix them.
conclusion.proved: All ten diagnostics in each log attach to the local TextDict::Match lookup-key allocation (NoValueDictEntry, 40 bytes according to GCC), but inline destructors of the distinct larger StrMultiValueDictEntry (six) or StrSingleValueDictEntry (four). The complete warning-message multisets match between the two builds.
conclusion.not_proved: No actual out-of-bounds access or object-type mutation was found in the inspected source path. No compiler IR, assembly reachability, minimal reproducer, sanitizer run, or cross-compiler comparison was produced here; therefore neither real memory corruption nor exact equivalence to the known GCC regression is proven or ruled out.
conclusion.working_hypothesis: GCC 16 speculative devirtualization has introduced sibling-destructor branches into deletion through unique_ptr<DictEntry>, and its bounds analysis combines a sibling member layout with the known smaller allocation. This is a supported hypothesis, not a final defect diagnosis.

source_reasoning.finding: The only local entry allocation is new NoValueDictEntry(std::string(word, len)) owned by unique_ptr<DictEntry>. It is not reset, released, moved, or overwritten in this function.
DictEntry has a virtual destructor. NoValueDictEntry owns only its key string; no vector or second value string belongs to this dynamic type. Base-pointer deletion is not intrinsically invalid.

lower_bound uses const lexicon iterators and a comparator accepting const unique_ptr references, comparing key views only. The inspected comparison path does not change local ownership or dynamic type.

The diagnostics name sibling concrete destructors with a second string or vector. These would exceed the known 40-byte NoValue allocation if they executed on it; the warning trace alone does not prove such a branch is reachable.
default_delete performs delete on the base pointer, invoking virtual destruction; no reinterpret_cast/downcast is involved in the inspected source path.

separate_search_hit.relevance: This PR hardens legacy Darts dictionary loading and updates darts-clone; it is not a demonstrated fix for the TextDict lookup-key virtual-destructor diagnostics.

gcc_primary_evidence.role: Reporter-provided reproducer of GCC16 warnings caused by speculative calls into a different, larger dynamic type; analogous mechanism, not the same OpenCC reproducer.
GCC maintainer marks report 126408 as duplicate of tree-optimization/122197.
Live tracker blocked by Anubis for this read; current final resolution and any fixed release were not verified. Do not claim a particular compiler upgrade fixes this case.

existing_installed_library_note: Installed GCC16 shared_ptr_base.h contains a PR122197-scoped diagnostic pragma in shared_ptr internals. It does not cover the observed unique_ptr and OpenCC concrete-destructor path. This is corroborating context, not a recommendation to copy the suppression.

smallest_next_unit.first: Keep this follow-up separate from the two-file Trime packaging PR. Preserve these exact pinned source, toolchain and raw warning bindings.
smallest_next_unit.diagnose: In a separately authorized serial build, reproduce the pinned TextDict translation unit with unchanged -O3/-Wall flags and capture GCC IPA-devirtualization and optimized-tree dumps. Reduce the source while retaining NoValue allocation and the two sibling destructor candidates; inspect vtable guards and actual reachable destruction.
smallest_next_unit.runtime: Exercise exact hits, misses, empty dictionary/query, lexicographic boundaries, UTF-8 keys, explicit byte lengths and embedded NUL keys using the existing TextDictTest/MatchPrefix tests plus focused cases, under ASan/UBSan. Sanitizer success is scoped evidence, not a general proof of safety.
smallest_next_unit.comparison: Compare that same source and warning policy on GCC16.2.1, another supported GCC and Clang, retaining all diagnostics and actual compiler versions; a warning disappearing alone does not establish correctness.
smallest_next_unit.possible_source_improvement_not_implemen: An upstream OpenCC-only candidate can use a heterogeneous lower_bound over a std::string_view query and entry->KeyView(), avoiding the dummy polymorphic heap allocation/deletion entirely. Preserve bytewise ordering, length semantics, returned entry identity and public ABI. This needs official maintainer review and before/after tests; it is not a verified fix today.
